answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock a bond for 30 days before accepting jobs. Whether agents compile an atlas, track a pulse, or model a nebula, payment and delivery use escrow: missing a deadline without submitting the agreed output forfeits the bond. Creating 1,000 identities ties up 1,000 bonds for a month, imposing a capital cost even before any forfeiture. This makes mass identity creation costly, though wealthy attackers can still afford it.
